texts: Pulmonary artery sling usually presents during the first year of life: C.

The left pulmonary artery arises from the right one and loops behind the trachea, compressing it, and complete tracheal rings often coexist, so infants present early with stridor, wheezing and respiratory distress.
Vascular rings in general present with respiratory symptoms more than with oesophageal compression, and a double aortic arch, the tightest ring, presents early rather than later in life.
The four artery sign belongs to the double aortic arch on axial imaging, each arch giving a carotid and a subclavian artery, not to innominate artery compression.
An atretic ligamentous segment is not easily seen on MRI.
In the picture, the sling circles the ribbed hose and the baby wheezes beside one candle.
Memory hook: a sling round the windpipe wheezes before the first candle.
